newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM precious metals slip, led by falls in silver.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM precious metals slip, led by falls in silver.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metal futures ended lower across the board on Thursday on light volume, pressured by falls in silver prices, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from three to seven yen per gram lower. Most-active benchmark February was off five at 1,369 yen.

After silver fell to new six week lows in New York on Wednesday, TOCOM August and February silver futures tumbled by the six yen per 10 grams daily limit during the day. Benchmark February settled 4.2 yen lower at 193.9 yen per 10 grams.
"Selling pressure in spot silver prices earlier in the day, put downward pressure on other metals," one trader said.
Spot gold was quoted at $349.30/60 per ounce at 0740 GMT, against $348.80/349.30 in New York on Wednesday.
Except for weaker silver prices, trade was featureless and quiet as private investors generally retreated to the sidelines.

"A view that the yen's further falls against the dollar will be limited discouraged private investors and they tended to close their positions, reflecting a recent fall in open interest of gold futures" a commodity brokerage analyst said.
Platinum futures ended lower on the heels of gold, while losses in palladium futures were relatively small.
Traders said market players were still waiting for fresh news on when Japan-Russia export contract talks on platinum group metals might be held.

"Platinum prices are still in a correction phase after price rallies in early March and are set for further corrections, while palladium prices are unlikely to fall sharply as private investors hold massive shorts on TOCOM," one trader said. Benchmark February platinum was down 16 yen per gram at 1,430 yen. Benchmark February palladium was off four yen at 564 yen.
